title: ICE Contractor ShadowDragon Collected Data From More Than 200 Sites
description_medium: A March 2025 investigation found that ICE contractor ShadowDragon could draw publicly available information from more than 200 websites and services, then help government analysts map individuals’ activity and relationships. A separate report documented ICE payments to Palantir for database modifications. The reports describe surveillance tools and contracting; they do not show that ShadowDragon powered the separate visa-screening effort or that every protester was targeted.
description_long:
On March 12, 2025, 404 Media reported that ICE contractor ShadowDragon had assembled a tool drawing publicly available information from more than 200 websites, social networks, apps, and services. A leaked site list showed that the system could help government analysts search data and map a person’s activity, movements, and relationships. The report placed this tool amid stepped-up immigration scrutiny of pro-Palestinian expression, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s announced “Catch and Revoke” effort to review student visa holders’ social media. It explicitly found no evidence that ShadowDragon or its SocialNet tool was part of that visa-screening program, so the two systems should not be conflated.

A separate April 16 report said ICE paid Palantir tens of millions of dollars to modify an ICE database and search tool. Procurement documents described “complete target analysis of known populations” and updated targeting and enforcement priorities. These reports document expanded surveillance infrastructure and contractor support; they do not establish that every protester was monitored, that political expression alone triggered deportation, or that the systems were used unlawfully. The cited records describe the tools, procurement, and stated uses, but do not verify specific deployments against named protest participants.
evidence_notes: 404 Media’s March 12 report says ShadowDragon’s list covered 200+ sites and states there was no evidence the vendor/tool was part of Rubio’s separate visa-screening effort. Its April 16 report documents ICE procurement payments to Palantir and the target-analysis language. TechPolicy.Press provides the broader dated sequence of monitoring announcements.
corrected_wording: Retitled to name the documented ICE contractor and its 200+ site data tool. Removed unsupported claims of comprehensive AI monitoring, direct targeting of all protesters, and a confirmed link between ShadowDragon and the visa-holder Catch and Revoke program.
